business: Aurelia, a generative wellness companion (web app; sessions made from one sentence)
target: Adults 25 to 45 who already reach for an app, a podcast or a YouTube video when they cannot sleep, feel stressed or foggy, and who would rather say how they feel than browse a library
where: Online, English-speaking markets (US, UK, Australia, Canada)

segments.name: High earner, already pays for wellness

behaviours.name: Free-app loyalist
behaviours.how: Uses free meditation apps or YouTube and has never paid for one.

behaviours.name: Lapsed subscriber
behaviours.how: Paid for Calm or Headspace once, stopped using it after a month, cancelled.

behaviours.name: Sleep-first
behaviours.how: Only opens a wellness app at bedtime, mostly for sleep sounds or stories.

behaviours.name: Sceptic of AI
behaviours.how: Distrusts AI-made content, especially for anything about mental health.

behaviours.name: Quantified self
behaviours.how: Wears an Oura ring or Apple Watch and likes to see data change.

behaviours.name: Tries new apps
behaviours.how: Downloads new wellness and AI apps early and talks about them.

behaviours.name: Therapy-adjacent
behaviours.how: Sees or has seen a therapist and uses apps between sessions.

objections: I already have free apps and YouTube for this
AI-made meditation sounds generic or a bit creepy
I don't want to type how I feel when I already feel bad
Another subscription I'll forget to use
Will it actually help, or is it a gimmick?
I don't want an app asking me questions every day
What happens to what I tell it about my mental state?
habits: you lie awake most weeknights scrolling your phone
your commute is 40 minutes each way with headphones on
you have a stressful meeting or deadline most weeks
you put kids to bed at 8 and finally have an hour to yourself
you track your sleep score every morning
you journal now and then but never keep it up
_grounding: Segments and behaviours are guesses informed by three user interviews (Oct 2026), the six-persona simulation (Oct 2026) and the Insight Timer review study (J089). Confirm with real people.
